claims.text: The ReAct excerpt reports that on ALFWorld and WebShop, ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by absolute success rates of 34% and 10% respectively, while prompted with only one or two in-context examples.

The ReAct excerpt motivates the approach by analogy to human cognition, arguing that combining task-oriented actions with verbal reasoning helps track progress, handle exceptions, and recognize when external information is needed.

The Self-RAG excerpt states that Self-RAG trains an arbitrary LM to generate fine-grained self-reflection tokens (via offline critic-augmented training data) that enable customizable inference, deciding when to retrieve and self-evaluating generation quality.
The Self-RAG excerpt claims its offline reflection-token training has a far lower training cost than RLHF and, unlike RLHF, enables controllable generation at inference.

The Self-RAG excerpt characterizes iterative LLM refinement methods (generate, feedback, refine) as costing inference efficiency, and positions Self-RAG against self-evaluation-guided decoding that covers only reasoning without retrieval.
